newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian sugar prices down on big supply - trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian sugar prices down on big supply - trade.

text.p: Russia's sugar market, flush with domestic and Ukrainian supplies and protected by duties, has little room for imported refined sugar from Europe or Brazil, traders said on Wednesday.
There has been talk in the London market that Russia might have bought up to seven cargoes of sugar recently.
"There is absolutely no reason to import white sugar from Europe or Brazil," said a trader at a Western firm. "It doesn't make sense."

Dealers at Western commodities houses in Moscow said depressed wholesale prices for Russian whites were running as low as $400 per tonne. Ukrainian supplies, including a 10 percent value-added tax, were even slightly cheaper.
Average Russian wholesale whites prices were $450-$460 per tonne, but varied by as much as $40 according to region.
Traders said it cost anywhere from $500 to $650 per tonne to bring European-origin refined sugar into Russia.
"Cheap ($400 a tonne) Russian sugar is available, but the quantity is not that big," said a second trader from a Western firm.
A Kiev-based trader said earlier that Russia had 600,000-700,000 tonnes of refined sugar, much of it from Ukraine, in warehouses.
Both Russia and Ukraine are facing poor sugar beet harvests, which in theory could boost demand for raws.
But three trade sources said they were not particularly looking for raws and would not do so until spring, when Russian supplies of whites traditionally run lower.
Total Russian duties and taxes on imported raws are about 11 percent, compared to a total 36 percent on whites.
Some Russian refiners, desperate for cash to finance tolling operations, were selling whites at what traders said was below production cost.
Ukrainian sugar for export to Russia could be found for less than $360 wholesale in Ukraine, with shipment to Russia and VAT taking the price up to around $400 a tonne.
"It is low quality stuff, but you can make jam," one trader said.

Russia's sugar beet harvest, according to preliminary figures, is a poor 14.9 million tonnes, below forecasts of 16.1 million and far below last year's official 19.1 million tonnes. Output may still rise on private farms.

Ukraine, a major supplier to Russia, expects refined sugar output to fall to 2.8 million tonnes this year from last year's 3.49 million tonnes, mostly on forecasts of a lower sugar beet crop of 26 million tonnes.
But Moscow traders were not cheered.
"The market is bad and sales are bad for everybody," one trader said.
